task.description: Implement REQ-162 strictly per the APPROVED design at lib/letflow/design/req162-lua-script-error-capture.md (passed CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR, commit 39f6bda). Read the full design doc before writing any code. In lib/letflow/engine/lua/executor.ex: (1) In run_script/3's existing rescue e in Lua.RuntimeException clause: keep the existing budget-exceeded string-match branch FIRST unchanged; when it doesn't match, build a script_error() value (design section 3) from the exception and the sandbox's grant set, returning {:error, {:script_error, script_error()}} instead of the current bare {:error, Exception.message(e)}. (2) Add the script_error()/lua_frame()/instruction_count_report() @type declarations (design section 3). (3) Instruction count: inspect exception.original for a populated %Lua.VM.State{} in its :state field -- if present, {:consumed, state.instruction_count}; if absent/nil, {:configured_budget, budget} using the same budget run_script/3 already threads as its own parameter (design section 2.3) -- NEVER a zero-filled instruction_count. (4) Stack trace: typed case (exception.original is %Lua.VM.RuntimeError{}/%Lua.VM.TypeError{}/%Lua.VM.AssertionError{}) uses Lua.RuntimeException.to_map(exception).call_stack; untyped/fallback case uses a fixed non-leaking placeholder message and an empty stack_trace list (design section 6). (5) Capabilities field: threaded as an explicit parameter to the shaping function, rendered via MapSet.to_list/1 -- run_script/3 passes Letflow.Engine.Lua.Capabilities.new() (the same empty set Sandbox.new/1 already installs today) since closing that wiring gap is explicitly out of scope (design section 4.1, OQ-1). (6) Add one new handle_yield_result/3 clause matching {:ok, {:error, {:script_error, _}} = result} returning result unchanged, symmetric to the existing budget_exceeded clause (design section 5) -- verify run_with_heap_limit/5 needs no change (design claims it already passes results through unmodified; confirm this yourself against the real code). (7) Extend execute_with_manifest/2,3's @spec return union with {:error, {:script_error, script_error()}}. (8) Add the new moduledoc section per design section 13 (5 numbered items). Do NOT touch platform.ex, capabilities.ex, or sandbox.ex -- design section 4.1 explicitly keeps the capability-wiring gap open, out of this requirement's scope.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: a test asserts an uncaught runtime error produces a structured SCRIPT_ERROR carrying a stack trace and capability state at failure, both asserted individually.
AC2: moduledoc states which restatement branch holds (instruction count retrievable via exception.original.state.instruction_count), naming the mechanism and citing REQ-148 section 5 by number.

AC3: a test asserts that when the count is not retrievable, the emitted event does NOT carry a zero-filled or silently-omitted-but-implied-present instruction_count -- the two-tag union structurally prevents this; write a test exercising the {:configured_budget, _} branch (e.g. via an exception.original shape with no :state field, like Lua.VM.InternalError if reachable, or a constructed test double).
AC4: the division-by-zero test uses 1//0 (which raises 'attempt to divide by zero' in this Lua 5.3 runtime), NOT 1/0 (which yields inf, no raise) -- moduledoc records this substitution and why.
AC5: a single test asserts SCRIPT_ERROR is pattern-match-distinguishable from all 4 other real arms (SCRIPT_FAILED, budget_exceeded, wallclock_timeout, memory_limit_exceeded) in one case/cond.

AC6: capability state is read from Capabilities.grant_set() (not re-derived); per design section 4.2, since execute_with_manifest/2,3's real path always uses an empty grant set today, prove this property by constructing a Lua.t() directly via Lua.new/1 + Platform.install/2 with an explicit non-empty Capabilities.new(["some:capability"]) grant set, bypassing Sandbox.new/1's hardcoded empty-set call -- assert the shaping function produces exactly that one capability in its output.
AC7: a test asserts the stack trace contains no '/' path separator or 'Elixir.' prefix in any frame's source/name fields (design section 6.3).
AC8: mix test and mix compile --warnings-as-errors both pass, real output quoted.

result.status: Implemented REQ-162 per the approved design (lib/letflow/design/req162-lua-script-error-capture.md) strictly: run_script/3's rescue e in Lua.RuntimeException else-branch now builds a script_error() (message, stack_trace, instruction_count two-tag union, capabilities) via new public-for-testing build_script_error/3 (and private helpers script_error_message/1, script_error_stack_trace/1, instruction_count_report/2), returning {:error, {:script_error, script_error()}}; added lua_frame()/instruction_count_report()/script_error() @type declarations; capabilities threaded explicitly, run_script/3 passes Capabilities.new() (same empty set Sandbox.new/1 already installs); added one new handle_yield_result/3 clause for {:ok, {:error, {:script_error, _}}}; extended both execute_with_manifest @specs with the new error member; added a new moduledoc REQ-162 section per design §13. platform.ex/capabilities.ex/sandbox.ex untouched, per scope. Wrote 9 tests in test/letflow/engine/lua/executor_test.exs covering all 8 acceptance criteria plus a design §7 regression guard; AC3 exercises the {:configured_budget,_} branch via a constructed Lua.VM.InternalError double (InternalError's real raise sites are unreachable from any Lua source that actually parses); AC6 bypasses Sandbox.new/1 via Lua.new/1 + Platform.install/2 with a non-empty grant set, per design §4.2. mix compile --warnings-as-errors: clean, no warnings. mix test test/letflow/engine/lua/executor_test.exs: 44 passed. Full mix test: 2283 passed (5 properties, 2278 tests), 3 excluded, 0 failures. mix letflow.lint_handoffs: 0 new violations. Routing to SECURITY-REVIEWER (this touches the capability/grant-set field and stack-trace sanitization, tenant-facing paths) then REVIEWER, per WF-02 Step 2a -- not marking this handoff PASS beyond ELIXIR-DEV's own scope.
